newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rattled resort begs 'quake god' to restore calm.
newsitem.headline: Rattled resort begs 'quake god' to restore calm.

text.p: A Shinto priest and 150 Japanese innkeepers made offerings of rice and sake to the "earthquake god" on Monday to plead for calm to return to their hot spring resort after more than 8,700 earthquakes in a single week.
The 8,777 quakes that have shaken the Pacific coast resort town of Ito since March 3 have not caused serious damage or injuries.

But some 80,000 cancelled bookings in the spa and seafood area 120 km (75 miles) southwest of Tokyo prompted the local business community to seek divine intervention before the April-May peak tourism season.

In a Shinto ceremony in which the offerings included fruit and vegetables as well as rice and traditional sake rice wine, priest Hideo Sugimoto bowed his head in front of a makeshift altar on a beach.
He appealed to the Pacific Ocean earthquake god to restore tectonic tranquillity and tourist traffic to the earthquake-prone area.
